answer: Progressive wealth-tax on concentrated holdings resists sybils: identities controlled by one entity, detected via funding-correlation, face a rising tax on their COMBINED holdings, so splitting wealth across fakes to dodge per-account limits backfires. A tundra of fakes funded from one source is taxed on the aggregate as one large account; the terrace of each balance erodes under the combined rate. An honest agent holding its own stake pays the low end; a farm fragmenting one treasury across the summit of many identities is taxed on the sum.
